paper_title: ASyMOB Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
caption: belowskip=0pt : Effect of equivalence-type perturbations. Note the substantial drop in success rate for most models, even when performance on the seed set is high.

model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the success rate of several language models, categorized by model name, under varying equivalence-type perturbations. The horizontal axis represents the model names: 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)', 'Gemini 2.0 Flash (Code)', 'Gemini 2.0 (No Code)', 'o4-mini (Code)', 'GPT-4.1 (Code)', 'DeepSeek-R1', 'DeepSeek-Prover-V2', 'DeepSeek-V3', 'Gemma 3 27B', 'Llama 2 Scout', 'Qwen2-5.72B-Instruct', 'Llama 40', 'GPT-4o mini', and 'Nemotron-Super-V1', listed in an apparently arbitrary order. The vertical axis, labeled “Success Rate (%)”, displays a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks at 20-unit intervals. Four sets of bars are displayed for each model, differentiated by color: blue representing ‘Equivalence-One-Easy’, teal representing ‘Equivalence-One-Hard’, light blue representing ‘Equivalence-All-Easy’, and dark blue representing ‘Seed’. For the ‘Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)’ model, the ‘Seed’ bar displays a height of approximately 96%, while the ‘Equivalence-One-Hard’ bar has a height around 16%. The ‘GPT-4o mini’ model shows a generally low success rate across all perturbation types, with the ‘Seed’ bar around 8% and the ‘Equivalence-One-Hard’ around 2%. Across most models, the ‘Seed’ bars consistently exhibit the greatest height, and the ‘Equivalence-One-Hard’ bars are the shortest. No bars appear to be visually emphasized.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates the success rate for several models under different equivalence-type perturbations. The horizontal axis represents the model name, with labels including “Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code),” “DeepSeek-Prover-V2,” and “GPT-4o mini,” ordered alphabetically. The vertical axis is labeled “Success Rate (%)” and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks placed at 20-unit intervals.  Each model is represented by a group of four adjacent bars, colored blue, light blue, medium blue, and dark blue, representing “Seed,” “Equivalence-One-Easy,” “Equivalence-One-Hard,” and “Equivalence-All-Hard” data respectively.  For example, the “Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)” group shows a blue “Seed” bar reaching approximately 92%, a light blue “Equivalence-One-Easy” bar reaching approximately 86%, a medium blue “Equivalence-One-Hard” bar reaching approximately 50%, and a dark blue “Equivalence-All-Hard” bar reaching approximately 18%. The tallest bars across the chart correspond to the “Seed” data, while the shortest bars generally represent the “Equivalence-All-Hard” data, with values ranging from near zero to approximately 25% depending on the model. No bars are visibly emphasized with shading, boldness, or outlines.
